 Learn more This could be the most important week of 2026 for AI stocks. Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL), Intel (NASDAQ: INTC), and SanDisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) are preparing to report earnings, and the results could determine where the technology sector heads next.In this video, Eric Bleeker, CFA, Chief Investment Officer of 24/7 Wall St., previews the biggest earnings announcements and explains what investors should watch as concerns about artificial intelligence spending continue to pressure technology stocks.After sharp declines across AI infrastructure companies, Wall Street is increasingly questioning whether the hundreds of billions of dollars being invested in data centers will generate sufficient returns.Microsoft's Azure growth, Amazon Web Services' accelerating revenue, and Alphabet's expanding AI infrastructure investments will be especially important. Meanwhile, Intel, SanDisk, and SK Hynix could provide critical insight into demand for semiconductors, memory, and AI hardware.We'll break down earnings expectations, the most important numbers to watch, and why this week's results could either reignite enthusiasm for AI stocks or accelerate the selloff. 
 Video Transcript 00:00 Speaker A One of the biggest tech earnings weeks of the year is here. Five companies will set the tone. Microsoft, Amazon, Intel, SanDisk, and Alphabet all report in the coming days. Now, we think this is the week that decides where the AI trade goes next. So let's dig into the details. 
 00:15 Speaker A First, a look back. Last week, the S&P 500 slipped 0.43%. The Nasdaq 100 fell about 0.8%. Those index moves may look small, but underneath them, artificial intelligence stocks sold off hard. 
 00:30 Speaker A Neo clouds led the selling. These are the companies that rent out AI chips, often with borrowed money. Over the past month, Core Weave is down 40% and Nevius Group is down about 31%. Debt concerns are spreading. 
 00:41 Speaker A Over the weekend, Elon Musk warned that debt markets have shut off for companies without substantial revenue outside AI data centers. Investors are also nervous about how much big tech is spending on AI, which has led to a flight from risk across the past month. 
 00:54 Speaker A The major tech companies reporting this week have felt the pain. Over the past week, Alphabet fell 6%, Sandisk dropped 6% as well, Intel lost 3.2%, and Microsoft and Amazon held up better, slipping 0.9 and 0.8% respectively. Over the past month, Sandisk is down 32% and Intel is down about 29%. 
 01:12 Speaker A Now, this week, interest rates will compete for attention given the Federal Reserve also meets this week, but the real fireworks for tech begin on Tuesday. That's when SK Hynix, the Korean memory chip maker is expected to report late on Tuesday night. 
 01:31 Speaker B Investors are watching how fast SK Hynix scales the HBM memory chips that feed AI processors and what demand looks like in 2028 and beyond. 
 01:40 Speaker B Microsoft and Alphabet are expected on Wednesday, October 28th after the close. Amazon, Intel, and Sandisk are expected on Thursday, October 29th after the close. 
 01:50 Speaker B Let's start with Microsoft. For the September quarter, analysts expect earnings of $4.72 per share on revenue of $90.71 billion. 
 02:00 Speaker B A year earlier, Microsoft made $3.72 per share. The big story is spending. 
 02:07 Speaker B Capital expenditures, meaning the money spent on data centers and equipment totaled $116 billion in the fiscal year that ended in June. That includes $35.80 billion in the June quarter alone. 
 02:18 Speaker B Last quarter, its Azure Cloud unit grew 43% and Microsoft 365 co-pilot passed 30 million paid seats. 
 02:26 Speaker B We want proof that cloud and AI revenue is keeping pace, and Wall Street will carefully study the company's spending outlook. 
 02:32 Speaker B Next, Amazon. Analysts expect $1.96 per share on revenue of $202.2 billion. 
 02:41 Speaker B A year ago, Amazon made $1.95 per share. So, expectations for profit growth are modest. 
 02:48 Speaker B Amazon spent $54.21 billion on capital expenditures in the June quarter, more than any other big spender. 
 02:56 Speaker B Amazon Web Services, its cloud unit, grew 37% last quarter. Its fastest pace in 18 quarters. Two questions matter most. 
 03:04 Speaker B Does the cloud speed up enough to justify the spending and does cloud growth keep accelerating at a rate Wall Street is happy with? 
 03:11 Speaker B Now, quick hits. Alphabet's stock fell 7% in July after the company raised its AI spending outlook. So the company's capital spending guidance is the number to watch. 
 03:20 Speaker B The business behind that spending is strong, with Google Cloud revenue up 82% last quarter. 
 03:25 Speaker B Intel and Sandisk tell us about PC, data center and memory demand. 
 03:30 Speaker B Intel guided for revenue of $15.8 billion to $16.8 billion and adjusted earnings of 38 cents per share. 
 03:37 Speaker B Its shares also rose last week after Musk signaled a breakthrough on his Terra fab project. 
 03:43 Speaker B Sandisk guided for revenue of $10.30 billion to $10.80 billion and adjusted earnings of $44 to $46 per share, helped by higher flash memory prices. 
 03:54 Speaker B Expect big swings. Sandisk has beaten estimates six quarters in a row, but it still fell 6.81% on the day of its last report. 
 04:03 Speaker B This week will tell us whether AI spending is bringing in enough revenue to calm the market. 
 04:07 Speaker B On Wednesday night, we'll watch Azure growth and how much Microsoft and Alphabet plan to spend. On Thursday night, we'll watch Amazon's Cloud, Intel's data center results, and Sandisk's pricing. 
 04:18 Speaker B If revenue keeps up with spending, the selloff has room to cool off. If it doesn't, last week's pressure likely spreads to the biggest names in tech.
